name: Noir
reference: Classic film noir: hard key light, venetian-blind shadow bars, black and white only.
pattern: Black, white and a few greys; no colour at all.
personality: Mystery. Hard light cuts across the type; shadows slide.

motion.character: Slow lateral pushes; shadow bars slide across the frame; cuts land on the beat.
motion.transitions: A shadow sweeps the frame dark, then the next scene is lit.

texture.note: Film grain and a slight gate weave.

grammar: One hard light direction for the whole film.
Shadow bars fall across type at a diagonal.

pictures.note: Hard key light, deep black; the shadow bars cross the picture as they cross the type.

footage.note: Slow black and white: rain, a stair, smoke through a blind.

music.feel: noir jazz, muted trumpet, upright bass, smoky

hits.note: A low hit when a shadow bar snaps; a soft whoosh as a bar slides.

compose.how: The lit plate fills the frame with the figure whole. Where the plate has a calm part clear of the figure, the line sits on it (lineOverPicture: never across the face or the body). Where the figure fills the text-safe area (lineOverPicture says dim), the line takes a band of the dark ground at the top and the plate fills the frame under it, its top eased into the ground (lineInBand, then photo with box: the picture box and fade: "top"). Keep the figure: a plate with no figure is the last choice.

hook.how: A lit plate with hard slats on frame 0, the first line already set in a lit band.

moves.move: Hard lit slats: the plate is dark, and only hard-edged bands carry the normal grade; type sits in the lit bands.

measurable.how: Hard edges at one diagonal angle cross the plate, and no letter sits in a dark band.

moves.move: One hard light direction for the whole film.
A shadow sweeps the frame dark, then the next scene is lit.

allows.why: Noir's shadow covers the frame dark for a moment before the next scene is lit: a few frames of flat dark are the move.

moves.move: A dark figure in front of lit words: the subject breaks the line and the line still reads.

measurable.how: Every letter keeps its contrast; no letter more than 30 % covered.

blocks.for: The subject cut out over the type.
The title at full measure over two lines.
The shadow that sweeps the frame dark.
A low hit when a slat snaps; a soft whoosh as a slat slides.

props.angle: the slats' fall; near-level (-6 to -15) when keepLit holds text of more than one line, so one lit band holds it
props.keepLit: the title's nodes, so every letter stays lit
props.exit: "fade" on the end card, with `until` on the last beat

blocks.for: Hard slats of shadow across the frame.

avoid.why: A noir title has no chart.

ends.how: The title in the light, the street in the bottom third; the slat light fades on the last beat instead of a cut to empty black.
ends.with: the title in the light on the last beat, held; `shadowBars` with `exit: "fade"` and `until` on the last beat fades the slats

mix.note: Smoky jazz. Cuts on the beat; the impact lands when the title is fully set, not before.

shots.match: One hard light direction and one grade in every shot.

subjectsToAvoid: Fibonacci numbers or the golden spiral
FizzBuzz or a sort of ten numbers
a detective in a trench coat with no story
